items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The bass was Louis Vola and Pierre Ferret who played rhythm guitar with Joseph.

ctx.x: It was a strange formation to me because it consisted of three guitars, a violin and bass violin. I had never heard any groups like them for the simple reason that none like them had ever existed. The violin player was the best I had ever heard playing jazz after Robert "Juice" Wilson on one, the guitarist was the greatest I had ever heard because guitars in those days, most guitar players played rhythm style. But this fellow took solos and had ideas and techniques that were out of this world.

The violinist spoke English and told me that his name was Stephane Grappelli. The solo guitarist was Django Reinhardt and the other guitarist was Django's brother Joseph. The bass was Louis Vola and Pierre Ferret who played rhythm guitar with Joseph.

Grappelli told me that Django and Joseph were gypsies. Django had had an accident with his left hand when he was younger and could only use three fingers. But he used those three fingers as if they were ten.
